# SolveGrid

> SolveGrid is an independent browser-based calculator platform focused on research statistics for theses and surveys (sample size, Cronbach's alpha, Likert analysis, t-tests, ANOVA, correlation), with supporting math, engineering, and numerical-methods tools.

SolveGrid provides 29 public tools. Most current calculations run directly in the browser and do not require an account. Tool pages are connected to method guides, related calculators, assumptions, and scope notes where relevant.

## Main directories

- [Homepage](https://solvegrid.online/): Research statistics workflow, featured tools, categories, guides, FAQs, and platform information.
- [All calculators](https://solvegrid.online/tools): Directory of every public SolveGrid calculator and research workspace.
- [Calculation guides](https://solvegrid.online/guides): Formula, method, notation, graphing, matrix, research statistics, sample size, Likert, and numerical-method guides.
- [Research statistics calculators](https://solvegrid.online/research-statistics)
- [Math and algebra calculators](https://solvegrid.online/math-calculators)
- [Scientific and engineering calculators](https://solvegrid.online/engineering-calculators)
- [Research and simulation tools](https://solvegrid.online/research-tools)

## Usage notes

- SolveGrid is independent and is not an official product of calculator manufacturers mentioned in educational comparisons.
- Results are informational. High-stakes engineering, medical, financial, legal, safety, academic, or research work should be verified using appropriate standards, source data, and qualified review.
- Numerical results can depend on rounding, floating-point arithmetic, step size, model assumptions, selected units, and entered values.
- Do not enter confidential, regulated, medical, financial, or identity information into general-purpose calculator fields.
